sections.heading: What is an AI Agent?
sections.body: An LLM that can reason, plan, and take actions — looping until the job is done.

sections.heading: Agent Architecture
sections.body: A request flows through the LLM brain, which picks tools to call. Results feed back through memory into the next reasoning step.

codeSnippet.code:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()
tools = [search_web, run_sql, read_file]

def agent_loop(task: str, max_steps: int = 10):
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": task}]

    for step in range(max_steps):
        response = client.chat.completions.create(
            model="gpt-4o",
            messages=messages,
            tools=tool_schemas,
        )
        msg = response.choices[0].message
        messages.append(msg)

        if not msg.tool_calls:
            return msg.content  # done

        for call in msg.tool_calls:
            result = execute_tool(call)
            messages.append(result)

sections.heading: Tool Calling
sections.body: The LLM outputs structured JSON that maps to real function calls — giving it hands to interact with the world.

sections.heading: Memory & RAG
sections.body: Embed past interactions into a vector database. On each turn, retrieve the most relevant memories and inject them as context.

left.label: Chatbot
points: No tool access or side effects

right.label: AI Agent
points: Takes real actions in the world

sections.heading: The Agent Stack
sections.body: Pick the right framework, guardrails, and eval strategy.
bulletPoints: Frameworks — LangGraph, CrewAI, Claude Agent SDK
Guardrails — input validation, cost limits, output filtering
Memory — vector DB for long-term, Redis for short-term
Eval — trace every step, measure task completion rate
